sanskrit: indrasya nāma gṛhṇanta ṛṣayo jaṅgiḍaṃ daduḥ | devā yaṃ cakrur bheṣajam agre viṣkandhadūṣaṇam ||
english: Invoking the name of Indra, the seers bestowed the jaṅgiḍa amulet; that which the gods fashioned at the outset as a remedy, a destroyer of viṣkandha.

sanskrit: sa no rakṣatu jaṅgiḍo dhanapālo dhaneva | devā yaṃ cakrur brāhmaṇāḥ paripāṇam arātiham ||
english: May jaṅgiḍa protect us — guardian of wealth, like wealth itself; that which gods and brāhmaṇas fashioned as a shield on all sides, a slayer of the foe.

sanskrit: durhārdasaṃ ghoracakṣuṃ pāpakṛtvānam āgatam | tāṃs tvaṃ sahasracakṣo pratībodhena nāśaya paripāno 'si jaṅgidaḥ ||
english: Those who come with malice in their hearts, with dreadful gaze, having wrought evil — them do thou, O thousand-eyed one, destroy with thy awakening power; thou art the all-encompassing guardian, O jaṅgiḍa.

sanskrit: pari mā divaḥ pari mā pṛthivyāḥ pary antarikṣāt pari mā vīrudbhyaḥ | pari mā bhūtāt pari mota bhavyād diśo diśo jaṅgiḍaḥ pātv asmān ||
english: Guard me from the sky, guard me from the earth, from the mid-air, guard me from the plants; guard me from what has come into being and from what is yet to be — may jaṅgiḍa protect us from every quarter and every direction.

sanskrit: ya ṛṣṇavo devakṛtā ya uco babhṛte nyāḥ | sarvāṃs tān viśvabheṣajo arasān jaṅgiḍas karat ||
english: The missiles fashioned by the gods, and those borne by the malevolent ones that strike down — all of these may jaṅgiḍa, the universal healer, render powerless.

sanskrit: prati gṛhāṇa pṛthivī nītam etad ājyasya mathitaṃ śarīram | imāṃ dhenum asya dātus tvaṃ rakṣa barhiṣy ā yathāsat ||
english: Receive, O Earth, this body brought hither, churned from clarified butter; do thou protect this cow of its giver upon the sacred grass, as it rightfully should be.

sanskrit: uta tvāhur varuṇasya patnīm atho tvāhur aditiṃ viśvarūpām | adhi jarāyum āghāre havyavāham agnāv asyā mahimānaṃ juhomi ||
english: They call thee too the wife of Varuṇa; they also call thee Aditi of all forms. Over the after-birth at the libation-pouring I pour oblation into the fire that carries the offering — her greatness do I offer.

sanskrit: sa sāhasraṃ tantum anv ā tatāna so agniṣṭomān daśataṃ sam āpa | adhijarāyuṃ savatsāṃ yo dadāti taṃ vai devāḥ svar ā rohayanti ||
english: He has stretched out a thousand-fold thread; he has accomplished ten agniṣṭoma sacrifices in full. He who gives a cow with its calf along with the birth-membrane — him verily the gods cause to ascend to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: adhijarāyuḥ svar ā rohayanty anena dattā sudughā vayodhāḥ | sāsmai duhāṃ śatadhāram akṣitaṃ yam asya loke parame vyoman ||
english: By the birth-membrane they cause him to ascend to heaven — the good-milching cow bestowed with it, bearer of vitality; may she yield for him an inexhaustible hundred-streamed milk in yonder world, in the highest firmament.

sanskrit: pūrvavatsena saha vatsinī gaur yo 'syā vatso aparo jarāyu tat | tṛtīyaṃ māṃsaṃ parinirmitaṃ yat tasmād devā adhijarāyum āhuḥ ||
english: A cow that has calved before, together with the former calf — her other calf is the birth-membrane; and that third flesh which is formed around it — for that reason the gods call it the adhijarāyu.

sanskrit: ā dhāvaya śavasā vāvṛdhāna- -uttarāva śrava ādhehy asmai | imam indra mahatāmena rakṣa saṃ prajayā tanvā saṃ balena ||
english: Run hither, O thou who hast grown mighty with strength — set thy renown upon him from above. Protect this man, O Indra, from great transgression; unite him with offspring, with his body, and with strength.

sanskrit: durvedāvastād bahudhā parastād viśve devāḥ prati paśyanty āyatīm | yā bhadrā yā sarvataḥ samīcī sed āhutir bhavatu me tarājyā ||
english: From the difficult-to-know side, from afar in many ways, all the gods behold the cow as she comes. She who is auspicious, who flows rightly on every side — may that oblation of mine be lavish with clarified butter.

sanskrit: gṛṣṭiṃ dhenum adhijarāyuṃ svadhāṃ kṛṇvānaḥ pra dadāti brahmaṇe | sāsmai duhāṃ śatadhāram akṣitam amuṣmim̐l loke yuga uttarasmin ||
english: He who performs the rite bestows upon the brahmin a cow that has calved once, along with the birth-membrane and the self-sustaining offering; may she yield for him an inexhaustible hundred-streamed milk in yonder world in the age that follows.

sanskrit: vatsaṃ jarāyu pratidhuk pīyūṣaṃ yo no dadāti sudughāmadhenum | tasya devāḥ pra tirantv āyuḥ sa ā rohatu sukṛtām ulokam ||
english: He who gives us the calf, the birth-membrane as the milker's counterpart, the beestings, and a good-milching cow — may the gods extend that man's life-span; may he ascend to the world of those who have done good.

sanskrit: parivālām adhijarāyuṃ yudhā jīvo adadāgra etām | syonā naḥ śagmā śivā viśeha mā no hiṃsīr harasā daivyena ||
english: The living man has given at the outset, in combat, the calf-encasing birth-membrane. Enter here pleasantly for us, peacefully, propitiously; do not harm us with divine fury.

sanskrit: bhadrakṛtaṃ sukṛtamādu śaṃbhuvam araṃ bhuvaṃ prati gṛhṇāmy āyatīm | ghṛtaśriyaṃ nabhasī saṃvasānāṃ devān manuṣyām̐ asurān utarṣīn ||
english: Wrought with good fortune, well-fashioned, truly beneficent, wholly apt — I receive her as she comes: she whose beauty is clarified butter, dwelling together in the two regions of sky and air — gods, humans, asuras, and the seers.

sanskrit: pañca devāḥ pra pibanta etām indras tvaṣṭā varuṇo mitro agniḥ | te sarve sam adur mahyam etāṃ tayeha jīvan pra tirasvāyuḥ ||
english: Five gods drink of her: Indra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni. All of them have given her to me; by means of her, living here, extend thy life-span.

sanskrit: kaśyapo 'yaṃ jamadagnir vasiṣṭha ṛṣayo naḥ sasanur agra etām | bharadvājo gotamo atrir naḥ syonāṃ viśvāmitro daduṣaḥ pra tirāty āyuḥ ||
english: Kaśyapa here, Jamadagni, Vasiṣṭha — seers have won her for us at the outset; Bharadvāja, Gautama, Atri give her to us as an auspicious blessing, and Viśvāmitra extends the life-span of the donor.

sanskrit: ūrjaṃ devebhyaḥ subhaga ūrjaṃ manuṣyebhyaḥ | ūrjaṃ pitṛbhyo aghnya ūrjā dadata mā viśa ||
english: O auspicious one, bring strength-sustenance to the gods; bring strength-sustenance to humankind; bring strength-sustenance to the ancestors, O inviolable cow — enter here laden with nourishment.

sanskrit: yā jātā oṣadhayo devebhyas triyugaṃ purā | manye nu babhrūṇām ahaṃ śataṃ dhāmāni sapta ca ||
english: The plants that were born three ages before the gods — I reckon now the tawny ones to have a hundred and seven abodes.

sanskrit: śataṃ vo amba dhāmāni sahasram uta vo ruhaḥ | adhā śatakṛtvo yūyam imaṃ me agadaṃ kṛta ||
english: A hundred are your abodes, O mothers, and a thousand your growths; therefore, a hundredfold do ye render this man free of disease for me.

sanskrit: puṣpavatīḥ prasūmatīḥ phalinīr aphalā uta | aśvā iva stha jitvarīr vīrudhaḥ pārayiṣṇavaḥ ||
english: Bearing flowers, bearing fruit, fruit-bearing and fruitless alike — ye plants are like victorious horses; ye are the herbs capable of bringing one across to safety.

sanskrit: oṣadhīr iti mātaro yad vo devīr upabruve | rapāṃsi vighnatīr ita rakṣaś cātayamānāḥ ||
english: As oṣadhīs — herbs — O divine mothers, I address you; crushing wounds and driving away rākṣasas, come hither.

sanskrit: niṣkṛtir nāma vo mātā niṣkṛtir nāma vaḥ pitā | sarāḥ patatriṇī stha yad āmayati niṣkṛtiḥ ||
english: Niṣkṛti — Release — is the name of your mother; Niṣkṛti — Release — is the name of your father; ye are swift ones, winged, wherever Niṣkṛti cures disease.

sanskrit: aśvatthe vo niṣadanaṃ parṇe vo vasatiṣ kṛtā | gobhāja it kilāsatha yat sanavatha puruṣam ||
english: In the aśvattha tree is your resting-place; in its leaf your dwelling has been made; verily ye are sharers of the cow, when ye win for the man his prize.

sanskrit: yad ahaṃ vājayann imā oṣadhīr hasta ādadhe | ātma yakṣmasya naśyatu purā jīvagṛbho yathā ||
english: When I, seeking vigor, take up these herbs in my hand, may the very essence of wasting disease perish — as a life-snatcher destroyed before it strikes.

sanskrit: uc chuṣmā oṣadhīnāṃ gāvo goṣṭhād iverate | dhanaṃ saniṣyantīnām ātmānaṃ tava pūruṣaḥ ||
english: The vital forces of the herbs rise up like cows issuing from the cowpen; the man wins for himself the wealth of those plants that are about to grant him gain.

sanskrit: yad oṣadhayaḥ samagmata rājānaḥ samitāv iva | vipraḥ sa ucyate bhiṣag rakṣohāmīvacātanaḥ ||
english: When the herbs come together like kings in an assembly, that inspired one is called the physician — the expeller of rākṣasas and the dispeller of disease.

sanskrit: aśvāvatīṃ somāvatīm ūrjayantīm udojasam | āvitsi sarvā oṣadhīr ito mā pārayān iti ||
english: Her who contains the horse-plant, her who contains soma, her who bestows strength, her who possesses surpassing vigor — I have found all the herbs, saying: "From here bring me across to safety."
